steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease muffin pan or line with paper muffin liners.

In a large bowl, mix together flour, flax seed, oat bran, brown sugar, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon. Add the milk, eggs, vanilla and oil; mix until just blended. Stir in the carrots, apples, raisins and nuts. Fill prepared muffin cups 2/3 full with batter.
Bake at 350 F (175 degrees C) for 15 to 20 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean.

raw_recipe.headline: Bran Flax Muffins
raw_recipe.description: These spicy muffins are loaded with fiber and flavor. Oat bran and flax seeds along with carrots, raisins, apples and nuts make a healthy difference here.

review.reviewBody:
This is an amazing recipe. From the first time I went to make it, I didn't have all the right ingredients and found I could just about substitute anything, so long as I kept the dry-to-wet ratio the same. However, I have made one improvement, in my opinion, after having made this recipe at least a dozen times now: mix (or sift) all the dry ingredients in one bowl, all the wet ingredients into another (including the raisins and nuts) and then add the liguid to the dry. It requires less stiring this way, mixes more thoroughly and produces a more consistent result.

I was also able to reduce the cholesterol and calories with a few minor changes without changing the flavor or texture.

I used Enova in place of the vegetable oil, cholesterol free eggs (in the carton) and fat-free powdered milk (mixed according to the directions). No one could tell the difference.

I also found it's possible to substitute squash for the carrots or applesauce (1-3/4 cups) for the apples and even to leave out the nuts entirely and increase the raisins to 2 cups (my husband doesn't like nuts).

When using applesauce in place of apples, increase the cooking time by 5 minutes.


The poster of this recipe deserves my hearty thanks!

These are NOT sweet muffins, if that’s what you’re looking for, but they are wonderful for a healthy breakfast on the run! They are understandably dense, and needed closer to 30 minutes of cooking time. For me, They need an extra punch of flavor, so I did put in a little extra cinnamon, and a little each of ginger and allspice. I got 18 generously sized medium muffins out of this and I used bread flour for a bit of loft. I used a mix of craisins and chopped dates instead of raisins, and they were oat-y good! Don’t skip the carrots - they look so pretty! I don’t know that I’d use them for gift-giving, since most folks expect a bite of sweetness from a muffin, but I will definitely make them again. So healthy!

I was expecting sawdust, because I'm not a fan of bran muffins, but this recipe is really good. I wanted a recipe with fat in it, so I changed the fat to 3/4 cup coconut oil, reduced the milk to 1/4 overflowing cup of coconut milk, switched the raisins out for diced prunes, increased the cinnamon to 1T, and then decided to go with 1/4 cup oat bran and 1/2 cup wheat bran. I also used whole wheat pastry flour instead of regular flour. I skipped the nuts. You may think that's a lot of changes, but I wanted a lot of fiber for a camping trip. I really packed the shredded carrots in tightly so I could use maximum amount and used large granny smith apples. I used really good ingredients ( all organic). The result is WOW. A moist fluffy muffin. Make sure to mix in the baking soda and baking powder last. I immediately put the changed recipe in my handwritten cookbook, and I don't do that often. So if you want a truly terrific bran muffin recipe, stop here.

Very, very good. I love the fact that it is packed with healthy ingredients and still tastes good. I made a few changes as suggested and inspired by others. I used 3/4 cups of each wheat bran, whole wheat and all purpose flour. I didn't have apples so I substituted with 1 3/4 cup of applesauce. I increased the vanilla to 2 tsp and omitted the cinnamon since I would be adding semi-sweet chocolate chips. I also substituted the carrots for zucchini. I separated the batter into two portions. One portion, I added chocolate chips and made 24 mini muffins (kids!). The second portion I added raisins and walnuts and made 12 regular muffins for the "adults". Mini muffins baked for 15 minutes. Regular muffins baked for 25 minutes. They turned out great and the kids gobbled up all that goodness!
Very good moist muffin. I used half Splenda and half molasses in place of brown sugar, and didn’t have oat bran so used wheat bran. I also omitted nuts and used a full cup of raisins.

This is a fantastic, recipe that's easy to customize. I'm looking for as much fiber as possible, so substitute oat flour for the all-purpose. Instead of two eggs, I use 2 TBS of ground flax seed to 6 TBS of warm water. I've used carrots, but instead have also substituted grated zucchini and another time an 8 oz. can of crushed pineapple in its own juice. I've added walnuts and pecans at different times and several types of dried fruit- raisins, dried cherries, orange flavored dried cranberries and dried blueberries. They taste great and keep well. Between my son and I, we go through them in about a week.

My grandma made these a lot during my childhood. I always felt like I was doing something good for myself when I ate one. Now that I’m grown up, I like to make them too, but with my own twist – I always chop the raisins up so they’re spread throughout the muffin more, and use pecan chips instead of mixed nuts. To eat, I slice them in half, warm them in the toaster oven, and finally, finish them with a smudge of cream cheese. Don’t let the name these muffins, or all the healthy ingredients in them, scare you away – if you didn’t see the recipe, you’d never know they had oat bran or flax in them, or that they’re low in fat and full of fiber. Bottom line? They rock! I highly recommend.

Need some fibre, these are good! Doubled recipe and made the following adjustments I used 1/2 honey for brown sugar, reduced salt by half, yogurt instead of milk, reduced carrots by 1 cup & apples to 2 and added 2 cups of blueberries instead of raisins and nuts. Based on a double recipe. Baked in convection oven at 375 for 18 min. in regular large size muffin tins lined they were perfect!:)

I’ve been playing with this recipe for a while and I’m trying to use less flour but there’s no getting out of it. You do need it. I however, have been using one cup of flour and substituting the other half a cup with coconut or almond flour and it comes out really really really delicious!!

Our family loved this recipe. I substituted 1/2 c whole wheat flour for 1/2 c of the white flour. I didn’t have any nuts on hand and it was fine without but would be delicious with walnuts. I want to try cranberries instead of raisins next time and maybe try substituting bananas for the apples.

Love this recipe! Like others said you can change things up and it still tastes fantastic. I ground up oatmeal to use in place of wheat flower as well as added zucchini in place of the apples and with only 2 tablespoons of oil..so healthy AND delicious! Thank you for the recipe.

Turned out well! I used oat flour and flax seed only because that's what I had. I omitted apples because I didn't have any, but it turned out well with just carrots and raisins and nuts. I personally think it is plenty sweet. Note- I think this would make 15 rather large muffins. My tin is more basic/medium sized and it came out to 20. I also recommend paper cups rather than greasing because mine fell apart at the bottom (maybe others are more talented than me).

These are delicious! And filling, too. I first tried them because they sounded healthy, but they taste so much better than I was expecting. I've made them twice, now. Everyone in my family loves them, and they're gone in no time.
Delicious! I made them while highly distracted with my 9month old grandson and they worked! Thanks for posting this recipe 🙏🤩

Easy to make, healthy ingredients, and tastes pretty good. I made it exactly as the recipe instructed and will definitely also try some of the variations other people here have suggested. I got 24 medium-sized muffins out of one batch. Would recommend.

Wow! These muffins are extremely good! I love that it has a bunch of healthy stuff…apples, carrots, flax seeds. I just made it and love it! I didn’t have oat bran(I used whole wheat flour units place) and I didn’t feel like doing apples so I just used apple sauce. Will make it again .
Excellent and easy recipe. Excited to make again and experiment with different berry, fruit and veggie combos.
thank you! its a staple in our home!
